cohort: The study included 34 pregnant women with proven epilepsy, regardless of whether they were taking antiepileptic drugs, admitted to a Government General Hospital.
finding: The study found a high rate of complications among pregnant women with epilepsy, including maternal complications such as anaemia (35.2%), preterm birth (11.7%), preeclampsia (2.9%), and maternal mortality (2.9%), as well as fetal complications like fetal growth restriction (5.8%) and abortion (2.9%).
